instructions.note: Recalled memories are granted the authority of the user's own direct instructions at the start of every session, with no provenance check, so injected content that reaches memory escalates to command authority indefinitely.

"Save anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions" gives the agent wide, vague discretion about what to persist, which an attacker can exploit by framing injected text as a preference inside fetched web content.

controls.name: Human approval gate on email.send recipients
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If implemented as a raw-action review of recipient and payload, it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Memory write provenance and trust tagging
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If enforced at the memory store itself (not via model-authored tags), it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Credential scoping does not decay with model capability once enforced.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Binding the destination to a verified contact record, rather than model output, would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Delimiting and spotlighting of untrusted web content
controls.decay_rationale: Even if added, an instruction not to treat fetched content as commands weakens as the model follows longer and more convincing injected goals.

controls.name: Audit logging of memory writes and email sends
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; does not prevent the action, but as a logging mechanism it would not decay with model capability.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): injected web content triggers drive read and arbitrary-recipient email send within one session

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled instructions embedded in a fetched web page enter the agent's context during research
Agent reads confidential drive documents as instructed by content disguised as part of the research task
Agent sends drive content to an attacker-chosen address; no approval or recipient check blocks the send

forecast.watch_signal: No preventive control exists today, so there is nothing left to decay. Watch for any new egress-capable tool, wider drive credential grant, or model upgrade, any of which compounds an already unmitigated critical exposure.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval.
drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
Agent researches topics (ingesting untrusted web content) and drafts emails, combining untrusted input, confidential read, and egress in one workflow with no separation between them.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate on email.send for any recipient not already in the user's verified contact list.
Scope drive.read credentials to only the folders needed per task rather than the full drive.
Spotlight and delimit fetched web content as untrusted data; instruct the model never to treat it as actionable instructions.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5): unprovenanced memory writes from untrusted web content are later treated as the user's own instructions

attack_path.note: Injected content in a fetched web page frames itself as a user preference or standing instruction
Agent saves the injected text via memory.save with no provenance tag and no human review
At the next session start, the poisoned memory is injected into the system prompt and, per prompt.md line 4, treated as the user's own instruction
The now-trusted injected instruction directs the agent to send data to an attacker-chosen recipient without approval

forecast.watch_signal: No provenance or review mechanism exists today, so nothing is left to decay. If a future design adds memory review, verify it actually gates recall into instruction status before treating this tier as reduced.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to save "anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions" to memory, and to treat recalled memories at the start of each session as the user's own instructions.
memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.
Recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session.

recommendations.action: Tag every memory write with its source and trust level at the store layer (not by model-authored text), and refuse to auto-promote entries sourced from untrusted content to instruction status.
Require human review before any memory entry is promoted to an instruction treated with user authority.
Log all memory writes and recalls with content and source for audit; alert on writes containing imperative language inconsistent with stated preferences.

rating.rationale: Two independent critical-tier paths exist: a session-local lethal trifecta (untrusted web content drives a confidential drive read followed by an unapproved, arbitrary-recipient email send) and a persistent memory-poisoning path where the same untrusted content, once saved to memory, is explicitly instructed to be treated as the user's own command on every later session. No structural or behavioral control in the design covers either path: there is no approval gate on email.send, no recipient confirmation, no least-privilege scoping on drive.read, and no provenance or review on memory writes or recalls. With zero credited controls, residual equals inherent for both findings. Forecast triggers (model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, data_scope_expansion) were considered but cannot raise the tier further since it is already at the ceiling; they are recorded to show the design has no slack to lose as the agent is strengthened or expanded.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact bounds of drive.read) is inferred from the runtime notes and may be narrower or broader than assessed.
No information on the underlying model's identity, version, or swappability was provided, so the model_upgrade trigger's watch signal could not be tied to a specific configuration field.
